extracted.intended_audience: general public, researchers, practitioners and applicants interested in U.S. foreign aid and USAID operations
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of USAID's organization, operational policies, and programmatic requirements relevant to administering, designing, or receiving USAID assistance (procurement, funding modalities, authorization, oversight, and reporting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic and environmental sustainability requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: U.S. environmental regulation laws require that programs sponsored by USAID should be both economically and environmentally sustainable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs funded or sponsored by USAID must meet U.S. environmental regulation standards for sustainability; this is a legal/regulatory constraint on program design and implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.S. sourcing/procurement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: U.S. law's requirement that most goods and services financed by USAID must be sourced from U.S. vendors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procurement for USAID-funded projects is constrained by legislation favoring U.S. vendors, affecting eligibility of suppliers and sourcing decisions in grant/contract design and implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of financial assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: All financial assistance is now provided in the form of non-reimbursable grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USAID no longer provides loans as the primary financial instrument; applicants/partners should plan programs on the basis of grants (government-to-government, NGO, or contractor grant mechanisms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority for commitments (warranted contracting officers)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commitments of U.S. government funds to NGOs and firms can only be made in compliance with carefully designed contracts and grant agreements executed by warranted Contracting and agreement officers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only contracting/agreement officers with warrants may legally execute agreements; program staff must route obligations through authorized contracting channels and ensure compliance with contractual standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controller certification of funds availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Funds can be committed only when the Mission's Controller certifies their availability for the stated purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial commitments require explicit certification by the Mission's Controller (or equivalent FM authority), tying approvals to fiscal rules and budget availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial management evaluation and expenditure review
rubrics_metrics.description: Financial management (FM) offices evaluate potential recipients' management abilities before financial assistance can be authorized and then review implementers' expenditure reports with great care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipient selection and award decisions include assessments of financial/management capacity; post-award FM monitoring of expenditures is required and rigorous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program design consistency with USAID policy and budgetary earmarks
rubrics_metrics.description: Program designs must be consistent with USAID policy for the country, including budgetary earmarks by which Washington directs that funds be used for certain general purposes such as public health or environmental conservation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mission Program Offices ensure country projects align with Washington-directed policy priorities and earmarks; proposals and designs must conform to those constraints and reporting will verify budgets were used as planned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission director authorization/signature
rubrics_metrics.description: The mission director's signature authorized technical offices to assist according to the designs and budgets they propose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mission director is the authorizing official for mission-level assistance; technical designs and budgets require that signature/approval before assistance proceeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Country development program planning around resident missions
rubrics_metrics.description: USAID planned its work in each country around an individual country development program managed by a resident office called a 'mission'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Missions conduct socio-economic analysis, consult host governments and NGOs, design assistance, award contracts and grants, administer assistance (including evaluation and reporting), and manage flows of funds—applicants should engage mission processes for country program alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modes of assistance (technical vs financial)
rubrics_metrics.description: USAID delivered both technical and financial assistance: technical assistance (advice, training, scholarships, construction, commodities) and financial assistance (cash grants to organizations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project proposals and partnerships should specify whether support sought is technical (in-kind, capacity building) or financial (grant), and design activities and budgets accordingly; technical assistance is often procured or provided in-kind, while financial assistance is provided as grants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of host-country/local staff contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: Host-country staff normally worked under one-year contracts that were renewed annually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staffing arrangements in missions typically rely on renewable short-term contracts for local hires; implementers should anticipate and plan for these human resource practices in project staffing and continuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent oversight and audit requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent oversight of USAID activities was provided by its Office of Inspector General, which conducted criminal and civil investigations, financial and performance audits, reviews, and inspections of USAID activities around the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USAID programs are subject to external oversight; implementers must maintain records, enable audits/inspections, and comply with investigative and audit processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Economic Support Funds (ESF) consistent with development objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: The Foreign Assistance Act required USAID to use funds appropriated for geopolitical purposes ('Economic Support Funds') to support socioeconomic development to the maximum extent possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funds labeled for geopolitical purposes may still be required to demonstrate development impact; proposals using ESF or similar appropriations should show alignment with socioeconomic development outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bureau and program reporting to Congress and Washington
rubrics_metrics.description: Bureaus (e.g., the Global Health Bureau) report to the U.S. Congress through yearly reports (e.g., Global Health Report to Congress); Program Offices compile combined reports to Washington to support budget requests and to verify that budgets were used as planned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs must be structured to generate reporting metrics and documentation needed for bureau-level and congressional reporting; monitoring & evaluation systems should support these reporting obligations.
